_comment: #1738 — mutation testing pointed at HARVEY'S OWN GUARDS, report-only (operator ruling 2026-07-31).
THE TARGET SET, and why it is this and not the repo. `mutate` is the registries and checkers that
decide whether some OTHER check is honest: ci-liveness (did a job reach its measuring phase),
alert-paths (is every alert path drilled), calibration (is the answer key still discriminating),
acceptance-conservation (did an issue close with a criterion nothing accounted for),
recorded-reasons (is a recorded blocker structurally falsifiable), scored-gates (does each
scored gate still have a cadence venue) and calibration-verdict (#1765's extracted verdict).
These are the files whose failure mode is silence: when one of them stops discriminating,
everything downstream keeps reporting green.
DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, so the omission is a stated decision and not a gap:
- detectors and semgrep rules. They already have better instruments than mutation testing —
a scored recall corpus (validate-calibration), a scored precision corpus (validate-precision)
and the OWASP corpora we did not write. A mutant killed by a corpus fixture measures the
fixture, and we already measure the fixture directly.
- src/cli/*. Their logic lives in the modules above; a CLI is argv parsing plus a print.
- everything else. A repo-wide `mutate` produces a BLENDED score, which CLAUDE.md warns is a
number measuring something other than what it gets quoted for, and it turns a report-only
census into an hours-long run nobody will re-run.
REPORT ONLY: nothing here fails a build. thresholds.break is null on purpose — see
src/guard-mutation-census.ts for the ruling and for why promotion is a separate decision.
